scope: Existing-host feasibility for source-supported tiny-counter repair at native16

bell.existingDslCapability: The source admission layer creates one part per SVG shape, so both subpaths become bell-outlined-0. DSL placement can transform only the complete part.
bell.result: The clapper cannot be translated or its interior clearance expanded without moving/redrawing the shell. No valid before/after bell repair exists in the current semantic DSL.

boundaryExamples.finding: The two link contours and horizontal connector are separate SVG shapes, so admission already exposes three independently placeable host parts. Existing placement can adjust their separation without raw paths.
Circle, stem and 0.01-unit cap-derived dot are separate SVG shapes, so admission exposes independently placeable host parts. Existing placement can adjust mark spacing while retaining the circle.

minimalSemanticApi.admission: Retain stable source-component descriptors for each parsed subpath: source part id, subpath hash, closed/open role, source bbox and paint rule.
minimalSemanticApi.dsl: Add a constrained component placement operation that references the admitted part plus a stable subpath hash and permits only spec-grid translation and bounded uniform scaling. It must reassemble the untouched sibling subpaths with the original fill rule.
constraints: No path coordinates or handles are author-visible.
Translation and scale values must use the selected master's legal grid and bounded tiers.
The host must reject unknown hashes, topology changes, fill-rule changes, and movement outside the source shell/keyline.
The checker must prove the requested native counter clearance improved while all untouched component hashes and shell geometry remain identical.

decision: Do not mutate the compiler from this probe. Implement the bounded source-component operation with regression tests before producing claimed bell or cross-morphology before/after proofs.
